## Join a newsletter platform that cares about your success – and won’t get in your way.
[Join your last newsletter platform](https://buttondown.com/register?utm_source=marketing-site&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=home)

"Nearly three years later, I’m still happy with that choice."

[Jeremy Singer-Vine](/blog/data-is-plural)

Creators just want to reach their audience, but why is that so *weird* right now? Social platforms come & go. Email providers grow and stop supporting you. Or they’ll shut down, despite the fact that you need your email to work like it’s a utility that you can depend on. Or they’ll hike their fees, forcing you to go through a stressful migration. Or they’ll add dozens of features that you’ll never want to use. Or they’ll just turn flatly evil.

This all should *theoretically* be easy: make something, tell your audience, repeat. And that’s how it *usually* is – until it’s not. Turns out **creating is only hard *when other people make it hard.***

We don’t. We *won’t.*

What if your email provider actually *wanted* you to succeed, and wasn’t trying to slowly bleed you dry? What if your email provider connected seamlessly to the places where you’re publishing new work, streaming, or just hanging out? What if your email provider didn’t change to support a few rich customers? Or they just stuck around *at all?*

What if you felt *good* about creating online?

That’s where we come in.

"I also frankly appreciated that [Buttondown] was just a newsletter backend service, and wasn't trying to transform itself into a full-on social network or curated feed. I've been around tech long enough to have seen how VC 'growth at all costs' pressure can deform publishing technologies. I didn't want to sign on with a place that was going to pursue that metastatic overgrowth."

[Clive Thompson](/blog/clive-thompson)

## The last email platform you'll migrate to.
Focus on your success

Focused on your success.

We prioritize our product roadmap from our customer feedback, not our own agenda. We use Buttondown for our own mailing lists. And we don’t take fees from your [paid subscribers](/features/paid-subscriptions).

The power you need

The power you need.

Our [automations](/features/automation), personalizations, and [editor](/features/markdown) help you send the right message to the right people. And if you want to try your hand at building your own tools, our [API](/features/api) is feature-complete & beloved in the industry.

Committed to the long haul

In it for the long haul.

As a small, independent business, we want Buttondown to be our life’s work. We have plans in place for the really long term. No, longer than that. *Longer.*

## And we're here to help.
Powerful for businesses and creatorsPowerful for businesses and creators

[Powerful for businesses.](/features/for/businesses)

You need your email to work. Fortunately, Buttondown’s deliverability is among the highest in the industry, and our spam protection is best-in-class. Our robust personalization & [automation](/features/automation) features allow your email to work for you. Our [analytics](/features/analytics) show you what’s working and how.

Got a large team? [Invite](/features/teams) everybody & collaborate on larger initiatives – with no per-seat charge.

Want to extend Buttondown’s functionality? Our [API](/features/api) will let you build anything you can dream of.

Powerful for businesses and creators

[Perfect for creators.](/features/for/creators)

No matter if you’re just getting started with a side hobby or you have an audience of millions, Buttondown will meet your needs.

Connect your email to [tools](/features/integrations) like Discord, Memberful, YouTube, and more. Skip login & post straight from your own email. Cross-post other platforms to your mailing list, allowing you to write once & [publish](/features/rss) everywhere. And if you ever need to leave for another platform, we get it – and we’ll make it easy for you.

We power single individuals *and* enterprise-grade businesses without compromising on either. That’s because **email, at its core, should be simple.** We put lots of effort into the most important parts of your email experience, because *that’s what you tell us to do.*

## Busy? Let us handle it.
Groaning about the possibility of migrating your whole list? Afraid something will get lost or broken?

That’s why we offer [one-click concierge migration](/features/concierge-migration) for your whole list, no matter how large it may be. Just create your account for free, [contact us](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#22515752524d505662405756564d4c464d554c0c414d4f), and we’ll get you migrated within one business day.

# Welcome to Buttondown!
Welcome to Buttondown, the easiest way to start and grow your newsletter. This guide will walk you through creating your account and getting everything set up.

You can also explore Buttondown's features hands-on using our [demo site](https://demo.buttondown.com).

[## Creating your account](#creating-your-account)

When you're ready to roll, [register for a Buttondown account](https://buttondown.com/register).

Buttondown is entirely based in your browser. There's nothing to install, so registration is quick and easy. You'll need:

- A browser with cookies, JavaScript, and in-browser pop-ups enabled
- An active email address that you know the password to
- A strong password for your Buttondown account

[### Choose your username](#choose-your-username)

Your username is part of your public Buttondown URL, so pick something unique and memorable. If you have existing subscribers that you're migrating to Buttondown, you may want to use the username they're familiar with. Don't worry, you can change this later if you need to.

[### Add your email address](#add-your-email-address)

Enter your go-to email address for receiving notifications, account updates, and billing information.

Later, if you decide to send your newsletter from the Buttondown server, your subscribers won't see the email address that you registered with. Instead, they'll see a Buttondown email address formatted as `username@buttondown.email`.

Sample email address if sending from Buttondown server

Alternatively, you can send your newsletter from a [custom domain](/hosting-domain). This is optional -- there's nothing wrong with using a common email domain like Gmail or Protonmail.

[### Create a password](#create-a-password)

Use lots of numbers, letters, and symbols. If you use a password manager that has a password generating feature, that's a great option.

After you've chosen a username, entered your email, and created a password, click "Create an account."

"Register" screen with information in all the fields.

[### Confirm your account](#confirm-your-account)

After you create an account, Buttondown sends a confirmation email to the email address you entered. Check your email for an email from "justin@buttondown.email" and click the link to verify your account.

Still waiting for the confirmation email? Check your spam folder.

[## What to do next](#what-to-do-next)

Now that your account is set up, here are the recommended next steps:

1. [Configure your newsletter's branding](/configuration-and-branding) -- set up your newsletter's name, description, colors, and logo.
2. [Build your subscriber base](/building-your-subscriber-base) -- share your newsletter URL, embed subscription forms, or import existing subscribers.
3. [Design your email](/designing-your-email) -- customize the look and feel of your emails with templates and CSS.
4. [Publish your first email](/publishing-your-first-email) -- draft, preview, and send your first newsletter.
5. [Share your newsletter](/sharing-your-newsletter) -- spread the word about your newsletter on social media and beyond.

If you're coming from another newsletter platform, check out our [migration guides](/importing-your-data) for step-by-step help.

If you're a programmer, check out our [API reference](/api-introduction) and [CLI guide](/buttondown-cli).

[## I need to talk to someone](#i-need-to-talk-to-someone)

Need help with your setup? Reach out to us at [concierge@buttondown.com](mailto:concierge@buttondown.com).

Want to report a bug, request a new feature, or just generally give feedback? Find us on [GitHub](https://github.com/buttondown/discussions/discussions).

Need to contact support? We're [here to help](https://buttondown.com/support)!

### Why are you so much cheaper than others?
You’re probably looking at other newsletter tools. Fair! And you’re wondering why those [charge a lot more](https://buttondown.com/alternatives) than us. Also fair! Maybe you think we’re not up to the demands that your business needs, or you think we’re not ready for “prime time.”

We’re cheaper than the competition for three reasons:

1. **We don’t maintain overhead.** We’re a fully remote, independent company. No fixed offices to blow rent on. No big initiatives that have nothing to do with sending email. We invest what you spend back into our business.
2. **We only charge for what you use.** Many email providers charge you for services that won’t be relevant to your work. We charge you mostly for active subscribers, and let you decide the rest.
3. **Most places overcharge.** It’s a sad truth that most places come to massively increase their prices down the road. We see no reason to do that. Newsletter hosting works best when it’s a utility, getting out of your way while helping you do your best work.

In short, we don’t want to overcharge you, even if you’re a big enterprise company that’s used to being overcharged. We want to give you the best possible service, no matter your list size.

### Do you have any discounts for non-profits?
Are you registered as a 501(c)(3) non-profit (or your country's equivalent)? You can get a 50% discount on your plan. Send us an email with proof of registry and we'll get you set up.

### Is there a limit to the number of emails I can send?
All of these prices assume that you're sending at most one email a day to your entire subscriber base. If you're sending more than that, you'll need to contact us and we can talk about what usage-based pricing would look like for you.

### Who runs Buttondown?
We're a small team of engineers, writers, and designers who are passionate about making emails better, fully remote and have been since our founding in 2017. We're profitable, self-funded, and have no plans to change that.

### Do you charge for active subscribers, or all contacts?
We charge for active subscribers — you only pay for the people who are actively receiving your emails.

### How do people feel after switching to Buttondown?
[Ask them yourself!](/testimonials)

### I have more questions!
Great! Send us an email at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#dcbfb3b2bfb5b9aebbb99cbea9a8a8b3b2b8b3abb2f2bfb3b1); we're happy to help.

It's been massively simpler & easier running things with Buttondown. Stuff gets queued easier, deliverability is higher, bugs are fewer.

Everything I needed was right there in the main UI. I could log in, write a newsletter, check it, send a draft to a friend for review, and then hit send.

# Fancy mode
Buttondown has a built-in [WYSIWYG](/glossary-writing-emails#wysiwyg) editor (in addition to the [markdown editor](/using-markdown)) that allows you to view and edit your emails in a way that resembles how they will be formatted when they are sent.

[## Built-in components](#built-in-components)

Fancy mode comes with a variety of different built-in components. To view the different options, use the toolbar at the top of the editor or type "/" on a new line.

A photo of the slash menu in fancy mode

[## Text options](#text-options)

In Fancy Mode, you also have a variety of text formatting options. This includes things like:

- Text color
- Font styling: bold, italic
- Adding a link
- Paragraph alignment: left, center, right
- Superscript and subscript
- Selecting a different font

To access text formatting, you'll select the text you'd like to format, and a tooltip will pop-up with the available options.

[### Font selection](#font-selection)

The available email-safe font options are:

- Inter
- Comic Sans
- cursive
- serif
- monospace
- default

[### Emojis](#emojis)

Emojis are fully supported in the editor.

Not sure which emoji to use? Simply type a colon (":") followed by a word describing the emoji (e.g., "happy") to see some suggestions.

**Shortcut**: add a footnote by typing [^text], "text" being any string sequence.

**Shortcut**: add a LaTeX block by typing your expression inside two dollar signs ($$) and pressing space/enter.

**Shortcut**: add a divider by typing 3 dashes or underscores & pressing space/enter.

[## Images](#images)

You can either upload your own image or use a stock photo from [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com).

[### Using Unsplash](#using-unsplash)

Buttondown has a built-in Unsplash integration, allowing you to search & embed high-quality images without leaving the app.

To search for images on Unsplash, click `Find image on Unsplash` using the slash menu and a modal will pop up. Search for the image that you want and click on it for it to be added to your email.

[### Uploading Images](#uploading-images)

To upload an image, you can drag and drop the image into the editor, or type `/image` on a new line to attach the image file.

[#### Adding a caption](#adding-a-caption)

Once the image is uploaded you can add a caption. This will appear for all readers, right below the image.

[#### Adding a link](#adding-a-link)

You have the option to make your image into a link. To do this, click the "Add link" button at the bottom of the image

[#### Updating alt text](#updating-alt-text)

[Alt text](/glossary-writing-emails#alt-text) is an important tool for visually impaired users to be able to access the content of your page, and also for search engine bots to index your archives. This text should be set on every image, by clicking the "Edit" button at the bottom of the image.

You can ask Buttondown to generate this text, or write your own. (Or maybe do a mix of both!)

The best alt text describes exactly what's happening in the image. Instead of "A cat in box", consider "A black and white cat staring straight ahead while sitting inside an open cardboard box"

[### Set class name](#set-class-name)

If you're using [custom CSS](/designing-your-email) you can set a class name for the image to make it easier to style.

[### Compression](#compression)

By default, Buttondown compresses your images to reduce the size of your email. If you'd prefer to turn this off, you can by clicking the "Edit" button at the bottom of the image.

[## Dynamic content](#dynamic-content)

Finally, you can add all sorts of dynamic blocks in Fancy Mode, including:

[### Webwall](#webwall)

A webwall enables you to add content that will only be displayed on the web. Any content below the webwall will not be included in the email sent to email clients.

### Webwall

[### Emailwall](#emailwall)

An emailwall enables you to add content that will only be displayed in the email sent to subscribers. Any content below the emailwall will not be included in the web version of your email.

[### Paywall](#paywall)

A paywall enables you to add content that will only be displayed to premium subscribers.

[### Subscription wall](#subscription-wall)

A subscription wall gates content in your [archives](/email-archives) behind a subscription requirement — any subscriber (free or paid) can see the full post, but non-subscribers see only a teaser. Unlike a paywall, it doesn't require [paid subscriptions](/paid-subscriptions) to be set up.

[### Subscription form](#subscription-form)

Add a subscription form to allow your readers to easily subscribe to your newsletter from within the email.

[### Subscription button](#subscription-button)

A subscription button is a [CTA button](/glossary-managing-your-list#cta) that links to your [newsletter's URL](/building-your-subscriber-base#sharing-your-buttondown-url), allowing people to subscribe to your newsletter there.

[### Free/premium blocks](#freepremium-blocks)

Free/premium blocks are a way to display content to your subscribers based on their subscription status:

- "Free-only" blocks are only displayed to free subscribers.
- "Premium-only" blocks are only displayed to premium subscribers.

### Free/premium blocks
Loading playground...

Loading editor...

[### Filtered blocks](#filtered-blocks)

Filtered blocks let you show a section of content to only one type of audience. Whereas a wall affects the visibility of all content following it, a filtered block only affects what's inside of it. There are five variants:

- **Email only**: visible in emails (hidden from the [web archive](/email-archives))
- **Web only:** visible on the web archive
- **Subscribers only:** visible to subscribers of your newsletter (free, paid, or gifted) across both email and web
- **Paid only:** visible to [premium subscribers](/api-subscribers-introduction#SubscriberType-premium)
- **Free only:** visible to everyone who isn't a premium subscriber

To add a filtered block, type `/` on a new line and enter a variant (for example `/email`), or click to add it directly from the menu that pops up. Filtered blocks also work inside list items and quotes, and survive switching to Markdown mode and back.

### Filtered blocks

[### Internal linking](#internal-linking)

You can link to another one of your emails via the normal link interface.

Either select some text and click the link button in the toolbar (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K), or type `/link` on a new line (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K with nothing selected).

From there, you can search your emails by typing in the link bar or select an email from the list below.

You can also search and link to another email by typing two opening square brackets ("[[").

Email autocompletion list in fancy mode

---

[### Snippets](#snippets)

[Snippets](/snippets) are reusable blocks of content that you can insert into your emails. Type `/snippet` or use the command menu to insert a snippet.

---

[### Survey](#survey)

[Surveys](/surveys) let you ask your subscribers a question right inside an email. Type `/` and search for one of your surveys by its code or question to insert it — Buttondown drops in the survey’s `{{ survey.code }}` tag for you. Surveys also render in transactional emails, like your welcome email.

---

[### Comments](#comments)

Comments are a way to add notes to your email. They are not displayed to your subscribers, but can be useful for you to keep track of your thoughts, or to share with your team.

[## Including audio](#including-audio)

Buttondown doesn't support native audio uploading like we do with images, nor do we have active plans on supporting it. However, we do have integrations with many *other* platforms, including:

- [Soundcloud](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/soundcloud),
- [YouTube](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/youtube)
- [Transistor](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/transistor)
- [Spotify](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/spotify)
- [Vimeo](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/vimeo)

Your best bet at the moment is to upload your audio to one of those platforms and then add it to your newsletter.

[## Including video](#including-video)

Buttondown doesn't host video, and dropping a video file into the editor attaches it as a downloadable file rather than embedding an inline player. For a playable video, the best approach is to upload it to a hosting platform and then paste the URL into your email — Buttondown will automatically embed a player. We integrate with:

- [YouTube](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/youtube)
- [Vimeo](https://buttondown.com/features/integrations/vimeo)

[## Attachments](#attachments)

Buttondown allows you to add file attachments to your emails, making it easy to share documents, images, and other files with your subscribers. Whether you're sending a PDF report, sharing a calendar invite, or distributing a resource, attachments make your emails more versatile.

[### Supported attachment types](#supported-attachment-types)

Buttondown supports the following file types for attachments:

| File type | Supported formats |
| --- | --- |
| Documents | PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, MD |
| Images | JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP |
| Archives | ZIP |
| Audio | MP3 |
| Video | MP4 |
| Spreadsheets | CSV |
| E-books | EPUB |
| Calendar files | ICS |

[### Limitations](#limitations)

Each attachment is limited to a maximum size of 1 MiB. This limit helps ensure reliable delivery across email providers. If you need to share larger files with your subscribers, consider uploading them to a file sharing service (like Dropbox, Google Drive, or AWS S3) and including a link in your email instead.

[### Adding attachments](#adding-attachments)

- In **Fancy mode**, type `/attachments` and select the file.
- In **Markdown mode**, drag and drop the file from your computer to the editor.

[### Attachment delivery](#attachment-delivery)

When you send an email with attachments:

1. Buttondown automatically includes the attachments in the outgoing emails.
2. Recipients will see the attachments displayed according to their email client's conventions.
3. For web archive views, attachments are available for download.

[### Attachments as a premium feature](#attachments-as-a-premium-feature)

Adding attachments to emails is a premium feature in Buttondown. If you have a free account, you'll need to upgrade to a paid plan to use this functionality. You can check the current pricing and upgrade options on the Buttondown pricing page.

[### Best practices for attachments](#best-practices-for-attachments)

Attachments can be tricky to get right without impacting deliverability. Here are some best practices:

- Keep sizes small: even though the limit is 2 MB, smaller attachments (under 1 MB) will deliver more reliably.
- Use descriptive filenames so your subscribers know what the file contains.
- Limit the number of attachments per email.
- Test before sending to confirm they appear correctly.

[### What's the maximum size of a file that I can attach?](#whats-the-maximum-size-of-a-file-that-i-can-attach)

Two megabytes. (If you *really* need more than that, email us and we might be able to figure something out for you.)

[### How many files can I attach to a single email?](#how-many-files-can-i-attach-to-a-single-email)

You can only attach up to 3 files in a single email. If you need to attach more, [please contact us](https://buttondown.com/support).

# Adding people to your team
Available on the[Professional plan.](https://buttondown.com/pricing?plan=professional)

Buttondown’s "Teams" tool is for anyone who wants to allow multiple people to manage a newsletter. Whether you’re looking to bring in a proofreading pro, a CSS expert, or an admin enthusiast, Buttondown makes it easy to invite friends and colleagues to join in on the fun of writing, styling, and managing your newsletter. There is no limit to the number of teammates you can have collaborating on your newsletter. Invite as many people as you need.

[## Prerequisites](#prerequisites)

Here’s what you need to create your team:

- A paid Buttondown account. Visit our [pricing](https://buttondown.com/pricing) page to find the plan that works best for you!
- A username, email address, author name, and description for your newsletter. To learn more, read "[Welcome to Buttondown!](/welcome-to-buttondown)".

[## Building your team](#building-your-team)

To get your team working together on Buttondown, you must invite them to join you and configure permissions that let them work on the right things.

[### Invite new teammates](#invite-new-teammates)

To invite new teammates to manage your newsletter:

1. Navigate to your newsletter's **Settings** and click [Team](https://buttondown.com/settings/team).
2. Click "Invite colleague". The "Invite a colleague" menu appears.
3. Configure permissions for your new teammate. You can read more about specific permissions [below](#permissions).
4. Enter your new teammate's email address.
5. Click **Invite.**

An invitation email is sent to your new teammate. In the "Teams" menu, their information appears with a "Pending" status.

[### Confirm new teammates](#confirm-new-teammates)

After you’ve invited your teammate, they’ll receive a notification email like this:

The invitation email includes a link to collaborate on your newsletter. Your teammate can click the link in this notification email to accept your invitation. If they already have a Buttondown account, they’ll be directed to sign in with their username and password. If they don’t have an account, a free account will be automatically created for them.

After your teammate accepts the invitation, they can start working on your newsletter. Their status will change from "Pending" to "Accepted" in the "[Team](https://buttondown.com/settings/team)" section of your newsletter settings.

Woohoo! Your Buttondown team just got a little bit bigger. Go ahead, add as many teammates as you like—the sky’s the limit! Just note that no matter how many teammates are collaborating on your newsletter, your "Author" name will stay the same. You can always change your "Author" name in your "[Email](https://buttondown.com/settings/email)" settings.

[## Permissions](#permissions)

You can determine the permissions your teammates can have across two axes: which *parts* of the newsletter they can access, and *what they can do* within those parts. There are four different levels of permissions that you can configure for each teammate. This allows you to give access to only the parts of Buttondown that they need.

They are:

| Level | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Subscriber management | Access to view, create, and delete subscribers, as well as analytics for subscribers. |
| Email management | Access to view and edit emails, as well as reporting and analytics on emails. |
| Sending emails | Access to send emails to subscribers. |
| Styling & CSS | Access to view and/or set the CSS, frontmatter, and other metadata for your newsletter or online archives. |
| [Automations](/automations-introduction) | Access to view and create automations for your newsletter. |
| [Surveys](/surveys) | Access to view and create surveys for your newsletter. |
| Administrivia | Access to settings, domain registration, billing information, lifecycle emails — pretty much everything not described above. |

Each of these (except for "Sending emails") has three possible configurations:

| Level | Description |
| --- | --- |
| None | No access |
| Read | Access to view |
| Read & write | Access to view, edit, and create |

[### Edit teammates' permissions](#edit-teammates-permissions)

You can change a teammate's permissions at any time. Here's how:

1. Navigate to "[Team](https://buttondown.com/settings/team)" and find the email address of the teammate you wish to edit.
2. Click the email address to edit their permissions.
3. When you're finished, click **Save.**

[### Revoke teammates' permissions](#revoke-teammates-permissions)

You can revoke a teammate's access to your newsletter. To do this, head back to the "[Team](https://buttondown.com/settings/team)" section of your settings, and click the three dots next to your teammate’s email. Select "Revoke," and your teammate’s permissions will update immediately.

1. Navigate to "[Team](https://buttondown.com/settings/team)" and find the email address of the teammate you wish to edit.
2. Click the three-dot **overflow menu** and choose **Revoke**.
3. Your teammate's permissions will update immediately.

[### Toggle between multiple newsletters](#toggle-between-multiple-newsletters)

If you’re on a team or two, you might be juggling several newsletters at once. But have no fear! Buttondown makes it easy to jump from one newsletter to another.

If you'd like to switch newsletters, click on the newsletter name in the upper left hand corner. From here, you’ll be able to choose a different newsletter.

Want to learn more about adding new newsletters to your account? Our docs on "[Managing your account](/account#adding-another-newsletter-to-your-account)" is the best place to go.

# Buttondown CLI
```
flowchart
  laptop[Local machine]
  buttondown_cli[Buttondown CLI]
  buttondown_api[Buttondown API]
  laptop -->|"buttondown pull"| buttondown_cli
  buttondown_cli -->|"GET /emails"| buttondown_api
  buttondown_api -->|"200 OK"| buttondown_cli
  buttondown_cli -->|"./buttondown/emails/hello.md"| laptop
```

The Buttondown CLI (Command Line Interface) is a powerful tool that lets you manage your newsletter content from your local machine. It enables workflows like editing newsletters in your preferred text editor, backing up your content, and syncing media files.

[## Installation](#installation)

Install the CLI globally using npm:

```
npm install -g @buttondown/cli
```

Or use it with npx without installing:

```
npx @buttondown/cli
```

[## What You Can Do](#what-you-can-do)

The CLI provides several capabilities:

- **Work offline** with your newsletter content
- **Edit in your favorite editor** using Markdown
- **Version control** your newsletters with Git or other tools
- **Sync content** bidirectionally between your computer and Buttondown
- **Manage media files** like images and attachments
- **Automate workflows** with scripts

[## Getting Started](#getting-started)[### 1. Authentication](#1-authentication)

Before using the CLI, you need to authenticate with your Buttondown API key:

```
buttondown login
```

You'll be prompted to enter your API key, which you can find in your [Buttondown settings](https://buttondown.com/requests).

[### 2. Pull your content](#2-pull-your-content)

To download your newsletters from Buttondown:

```
buttondown pull
```

This creates a `./buttondown` directory with all your content.

[### 3. Create or edit newsletters](#3-create-or-edit-newsletters)

Create a new draft:

```
buttondown create --title="My Newsletter Issue #1"
```

Then edit the created Markdown file with your preferred editor.

[### 4. Push your changes](#4-push-your-changes)

When you're ready to save your changes back to Buttondown:

```
buttondown push
```

**Important:** `buttondown push` **doesn't** publish emails with the `status: draft` field, which is the default status for new emails. See the [Publishing Behavior](#publishing-behavior) section below for details on how to actually send your emails.

[## Publishing Behavior](#publishing-behavior)

When you run `buttondown push`, it syncs your content to Buttondown maintaining the status in the frontmatter. Here's how publishing works:

[### Status Field Controls Publishing](#status-field-controls-publishing)

The `status` field in your email's frontmatter determines what happens:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | Email remains a draft when pushed |
| `scheduled` | Email **will be sent** at the specified `publish_date` |
| `about_to_send` | Email is queued and **will be sent** very soon (typically within a few minutes) |
| `sent` | Email has already been sent -- editing these will change their body in the archives |

More information on statuses is available in the [API reference](/api-emails-introduction#status).

[## Directory Structure](#directory-structure)

The CLI creates this structure in your local folder:

### Directory Structure
buttondown/Project root directory

.buttondown.jsonConfiguration and sync tracking

emails/Newsletter content as Markdown

media/Images and attachments

[## Newsletter Format](#newsletter-format)

Each newsletter is stored as a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter:

```
---
id: email-id
subject: My Newsletter Issue #1
status: draft
email_type: public
slug: newsletter-issue-1
publish_date: 2023-04-27T09:00:00Z
created: 2023-04-25T15:32:18Z
modified: 2023-04-26T10:45:22Z
description: A brief description of this newsletter issue for SEO and archives
image: https://placecats.com/1200/630
attachments:
  - attachment-id-1
  - attachment-id-2
---

# My Newsletter Issue #1

Hello subscribers!

This is the content of my email...
```

[## Email Fields Reference](#email-fields-reference)[### Required Fields](#required-fields)

When creating emails via the CLI, only **one field is truly required**:

| Field | Type | Description | Required When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `string` | The email subject line | **Always required** for API creation |
| `title` | `string` | Used by CLI `create` command (becomes `subject`) | Required for `buttondown create` command |

[### Optional Fields](#optional-fields)

All other fields are optional and have sensible defaults:

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `string` | `""` | Email content (HTML or Markdown) |
| `status` | `string` | `"about_to_send"` | Email status |
| `email_type` | `string` | `"public"` | Email visibility type |
| `slug` | `string` | `null` | URL-friendly identifier |
| `description` | `string` | `""` | Human-readable description |
| `image` | `string` | `""` | Primary image URL |
| `publish_date` | `datetime` | `null` | Scheduled publish date |
| `attachments` | `array<UUID>` | `[]` | List of attachment IDs |
| `metadata` | `object` | `{}` | Custom metadata fields |
| `canonical_url` | `string` | `""` | Original content URL |
| `secondary_id` | `integer` | `null` | Informal issue number |
| `filters` | `object` | `FilterGroup()` | Subscriber filtering rules |
| `commenting_mode` | `string` | `"enabled"` | Comment settings |
| `related_email_ids` | `array<string>` | `[]` | Related email IDs |
| `featured` | `boolean` | `false` | Archive highlighting |

[### Email Type Values](#email-type-values)

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `public` | Visible to all subscribers and in archives |
| `private` | Only visible to subscribers |
| `premium` | Only visible to paid subscribers |
| `free` | Only visible to free subscribers |
| `churned` | Only visible to churned subscribers |
| `archival` | For imported/archived content |

[### Email Status Values](#email-status-values)

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | Email is being composed |
| `about_to_send` | Email is ready to send |
| `scheduled` | Email is scheduled for future |
| `in_flight` | Email is currently sending |
| `sent` | Email has been sent |
| `paused` | Sending was paused |
| `imported` | Email was imported from external source |

[### Validation Rules](#validation-rules)[#### Subject Line](#subject-line)

- **Maximum length**: 1000 characters
- **XSS validation**: Subject is validated against XSS attacks
- **Required**: Cannot be empty when creating via API

[#### Body Content](#body-content)

- **Format**: Accepts HTML or Markdown
- **Null characters**: Not allowed in body content
- **XSS validation**: Body is validated against XSS attacks
- **Default**: Empty string if not provided

[#### Slug](#slug)

- **Format**: Must be URL-safe (validated with Django's `validate_slug`)
- **Maximum length**: 100 characters
- **Uniqueness**: Must be unique within the newsletter
- **Auto-generation**: Generated from subject if not provided

[### Common Email Examples](#common-email-examples)[#### Creating a Newsletter Issue](#creating-a-newsletter-issue)

```
---
subject: "Newsletter #42: The Ultimate Question"
email_type: public
status: draft
slug: newsletter-42-ultimate-question
description: "Our 42nd newsletter covering the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything"
---

# Newsletter #42: The Ultimate Question

Welcome to our 42nd newsletter...
```

[#### Scheduling an Email](#scheduling-an-email)

```
---
subject: "Weekly Digest - January 17, 2024"
email_type: public
status: scheduled
publish_date: 2024-01-17T15:00:00.000Z
---

# Weekly Digest

This week's highlights...
```

[#### Premium Content](#premium-content)

```
---
subject: "Premium Analysis: Market Trends"
email_type: premium
status: about_to_send
description: "Deep dive analysis available only to premium subscribers"
---

# Premium Analysis: Market Trends

Dear premium subscribers...
```

[## Common Workflows](#common-workflows)[### Working with Existing Content](#working-with-existing-content)

```
# Create a directory for your newsletter
mkdir my-newsletter
cd my-newsletter

# Pull all your content from Buttondown
buttondown pull
```

[### Editing and Publishing Workflow](#editing-and-publishing-workflow)

```
# Pull latest changes
buttondown pull

# Create a new draft
buttondown create --title="This Week's Update"

# Edit the file in your editor
# Push to save as draft
buttondown push

# When ready to send, edit frontmatter to set status: scheduled
# Then push again to schedule the email
buttondown push
```

[### Adding Images](#adding-images)

1. Add images to the `media/` directory
2. Reference them in your Markdown:

```
![My Image](../media/my-image.png)
```

3. When you `buttondown push`, the CLI uploads the images and updates the URLs

[### Backing Up Your Content](#backing-up-your-content)

```
mkdir buttondown-backup
cd buttondown-backup
buttondown pull
```

Consider adding this to a scheduled task for regular backups.

[## Advanced Usage](#advanced-usage)[### Working with Multiple Newsletters](#working-with-multiple-newsletters)

You can work with different newsletters using different directories:

```
buttondown pull --directory=./newsletter1
buttondown pull --directory=./newsletter2
```

[### Using with Git](#using-with-git)

```
# Initialize a Git repository
git init

# Pull content from Buttondown
buttondown pull

# Add and commit the files
git add .
git commit -m "Initial import from Buttondown"
```

[### Automating with Scripts](#automating-with-scripts)

Create a script like `publish.sh`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# Pull latest changes
buttondown pull

# Create a new draft with today's date
TITLE="Newsletter $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
buttondown create --title="$TITLE"

# Open in your editor
code ./buttondown/emails/
```

Make it executable with `chmod +x publish.sh`

[## Available Commands](#available-commands)

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `buttondown login` | Authenticate with Buttondown |
| `buttondown logout` | Clear stored credentials |
| `buttondown pull` | Download content from Buttondown |
| `buttondown push` | Upload content to Buttondown |
| `buttondown create` | Create a new draft email locally |

[## Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)[### API Key Issues](#api-key-issues)

If you encounter authentication errors:

```
buttondown logout
buttondown login
```

[### Sync Conflicts](#sync-conflicts)

If you've modified the same email both locally and on Buttondown:

1. Back up your local changes: `cp -r ./buttondown ./buttondown-backup`
2. Pull fresh content: `buttondown pull --force`
3. Manually merge the differences
4. Push the resolved content: `buttondown push`

[### Common Error Messages](#common-error-messages)

The CLI provides specific error messages for common issues:

- **Missing title**: `Error: --title is required for the create command`
- **Invalid format**: `Skipping [file]: Invalid format (missing frontmatter)`
- **Upload failures**: `Failed to upload image [filename]: [error message]`
- **API errors**: `Failed to create email: [error details]`

[## Getting Help](#getting-help)

For more information, contact [Buttondown support](mailto:support@buttondown.com).

## Everything you need. Nothing you don't.
Paid Subscriptions.

### Paid Subscriptions.
Charge for your newsletter however you'd like. Ask readers to name their own price. Set up a free tier.
The best part? We won't charge you extra for paid subscribers, so you'll keep all of the revenue that you make.

[Learn more →](/features/paid-subscriptions)

Automations.

### Automations.
Our automations help you turbocharge your relationships at scale.
Build custom sequences for new subscribers. Create flows for tagged subscribers. Survey customers to personalize their content. Control exactly when & how each email is sent.

[Learn more →](/features/automation)

Analytics and privacy.

### Analytics and privacy.
Buttondown is GDPR-compliant and then some. We don't collect any data about you or your subscribers by default.
Want a closer look into subscriber behavior & email performance? It's available in one click, giving you the right insights at a glance.

[Learn more →](/features/analytics)

Concierge migration.

### Concierge migration.
Overwhelmed by the prospect of switching mailing list providers? We'll migrate your list to Buttondown for free, no matter how large it is.
Yes, really. No, there isn't a catch.

[Learn more →](/features/concierge-migration)

[Integrations.](/features/integrations)

Buttondown connects with your whole marketing & tech system to make sure that you're making the most out of every email you send – seamlessly & without fuss.

## Are you a nerd? So are we.
Connect Buttondown to other apps. Tweak your email flows however you need. Write how you like to write.

Screenshot of Markdown. feature

[Markdown.](/features/markdown)

Our editor supports native Markdown for you to write emails faster & with fewer errors.

New to Markdown? It takes only a few minutes to learn. We've helped thousands.

Screenshot of RSS. feature

[RSS.](/features/rss)

Not only can we publish your list as an RSS feed, but we can also take your existing blog's RSS and turn it into a mailing list – published at any frequency you'd like.

Screenshot of First-party API. feature

[First-party API.](/features/api)

Part of being technical means you need a great API. Ours is a great API. Supercharge your newsletter with our well-documented, webhook-filled REST API – whatever you can do on the app, you can do there.

## There's more.
We're actively building Buttondown to be the best simple email tool.

### Comments.
Let people comment on your posts – or not.

Email is great. *Replies* to your emails are great, too. But what if you want your subscribers to read what each other has written, and talk to one another?

Buttondown's built-in comments interface gives your favorite readers a place to talk with each other and stay connected with you.

Unlike other email providers, comments are a first-party feature of Buttondown, and you can build [automations](/features/automation) & [integrations](/features/integrations) for them just like you would any other part of your newsletter.

### Surveys.
Ask your audience. Track responses. Find new ways to engage.

Want to know what your audience thinks? Our surveys allow you to gather valuable feedback, conduct polls, and gain insights to tailor your content and improve your newsletter.

Subscribers answer straight in their browser, which improves completion rates. You'll get the results in your inbox and your analytics pages.

Buttondown's surveys boast response rates *200%* higher than the industry average. Why? Because they're easy to answer, and they're sent from a trusted source. Subscribers don't have to click through to a third-party site, and they don't have to worry about their data being sold to advertisers.

### Sponsorships.
Sell ad slots in your newsletter. We handle the booking, you handle the writing.

Set the prices, the format, and the dates. Sponsors browse your available slots, pay through Stripe, and submit their content themselves — you approve it before it goes out.

Buttondown doesn't take a cut: you keep 100% of every sponsorship (minus Stripe's processing fee). See the full breakdown on the [sponsorships page](/features/sponsorships).

### Attachments.
Include anything with your emails.

Enhance your newsletters by attaching files, documents, or any other relevant content. Share resources, exclusive content, or supplementary materials with ease.

Need to embed videos, GIFs, songs, ~~tweets~~ posts, or anything else? We support [over 40 integrations](/features/integrations).

### Send from your own email.
Post to Buttondown from your personal or business email account.

Want to send your newsletter straight from your email client? You can – while maintaining a consistent, professional appearance.

Send an email to `[email protected]` from the email address that you joined Buttondown with, and we'll send it out to your subscribers. Want to save it as a draft? Send it to`[email protected]` instead.

### CLI.
Draft, schedule, and analyze emails without leaving your terminal.

Write in Vim, VS Code, or whatever editor you like. Keep your drafts in Git alongside your code, and sync them to Buttondown when they're ready.

Script your newsletter from CI/CD pipelines, bulk-manage subscribers, and pull analytics — if you can do it in the web app, you can do it from the command line. See the [CLI page](/features/cli) for more.

### Unlimited newsletters.
Create as many distinct newsletters as you'd like – you're only charged for your total subscribers.

Expand your reach with multiple newsletters tailored to different audiences or topics. Our flexible pricing model ensures you only pay based on your total subscriber count, not the number of newsletters.

### Archives.
Post your newsletters to the web. Share them far & wide.

Yes, we mostly send *email*. But sometimes you'll want to share a permalink of your content, or have people browse your newsletter's archives.

Many of our competitors have this functionality, and people have come to expect it. But many still don't. For those of you who are switching from them, or who are considering switching based on having publicly-facing archives, rest assured: we have them.

Hide specific emails if you need. Set up a paywall for your [paid](https://buttondown.com/features/paid-subscriptions) content. And if you don't *want* them for whatever reason, you can turn them off, and just stick to sending email. Easy.

### Unlimited contributors.
Invite your whole team. Get help managing your lists with unlimited contributor accounts.

Collaborate effortlessly with your team. Add as many contributors as you need to help manage, create, and send newsletters, fostering a truly collaborative environment for your content creation.

You can set specific permissions for each contributor, so you can control what they can and can't do.

Wondering where a feature is that we might be missing? [Reach out.](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#89fafcf9f9e6fbfdc9ebfcfdfde6e7ede6fee7a7eae6e4) We're here to serve you, and we use your feedback to build our roadmap.

## Buttondown has a pleasant REST API to let you supercharge your newsletter.
Everything you can do in Buttondown, you can do with the API. [Manage subscribers](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-subscribers-introduction), [send emails](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-emails-introduction), [create automations](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-automation-introduction) — all from your own code.

[Show me the damn docs](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction)

Here are some common operations to get you started.

Send broadcast emailSend transactional emailCreate a subscriberCreate a newsletter

```
import requests

url = "https://api.buttondown.com/v1/emails"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Token $BUTTONDOWN_API_KEY",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
data = {
    "subject": "Weekly Newsletter - Product Updates",
    "body": """# Product Updates This Week

Hey everyone! Here's what's new:

## New Features
- **Advanced Analytics**: Track subscriber engagement like never before
- **Custom Templates**: Create your own email designs
- **API Improvements**: Faster response times and better error handling

## Coming Soon
- Mobile app for iOS and Android
- Advanced automation workflows
- Integration with 50+ popular tools

Thanks for being part of our community!

Best,
The Team""",
    "status": "sent"
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=data)
print(response.json())
```

## Build whatever you need.
The [interface](/features/markdown) and [integrations like Zapier](/features/integrations) handle most use cases. But when you need something custom, the API is there:

- **Power your SaaS.** Programmatically [send emails](https://docs.buttondown.com/scheduling-emails-via-the-api), [manage subscribers](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-subscribers-introduction), and handle [paid subscriptions](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-subscribers-stripe-subscriptions) from your own application.
- **Integrate with your stack.** Connect Buttondown to your [analytics](https://docs.buttondown.com/retrieving-analytics-data), CRM, or any internal tool.
- **Automate everything.** Sync [subscriber data](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-subscribers-automations), [trigger emails from external events](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-webhooks-event-types), or build your own dashboard.

## API-first by design.
We didn't bolt on an API after the fact. Every feature in Buttondown is built [API-first](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction) — we use the same API to power our own app. Open your browser's network tab and see for yourself.

That means no second-class endpoints, no missing functionality, and no surprises. If you can click it, you can script it.

### Is the API available on the free plan?
Yes. The API is available on all plans, including free. Learn more about [getting started with the API](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction).

### Is there a rate limit?
Yes. The API is rate-limited to prevent abuse, but the limits are generous enough for most use cases. Learn more about [rate limits](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-rate-limits).

### Where do I find my API key?
On the [API keys page](https://buttondown.com/keys) in your Buttondown account. You can also create multiple API keys with different permissions.

### Do you have an official SDK for my language?
No, and that's deliberate. We'd rather invest in making our [OpenAPI spec](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction) as good as humanly possible — which benefits every caller regardless of language or framework — than maintain a fleet of SDKs that inevitably lag behind the API itself. Every SDK encodes a pile of subjective decisions (error handling, pagination ergonomics, retry semantics, naming conventions) that we'd rather leave to you. If you want a typed client, generators like [openapi-typescript](https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript) or [openapi-python-client](https://github.com/openapi-generators/openapi-python-client) will give you one in seconds.

### Do you have an MCP server?
No, for essentially the same reasons we don't ship official SDKs: an MCP server is a thin, opinionated wrapper around our API, and we'd rather keep refining the [OpenAPI spec](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction) underneath so every caller benefits. If you want one, point Claude (or your LLM of choice) at our [API spec](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction) and ask it to build an MCP server tailored to your workflow — you'll end up with something better-fit than anything we could ship generically.

## Buttondown has full-fledged Markdown support with some extra fun stuff, too.
For many people, your editor is the center of an email tool. Our editor is best-in-class, allowing you to write WYSIWYG with rich text – *and* in Markdown, the lightning-fast language that has become standard throughout the industry.

While there are some additional features, they are tucked away nicely, allowing me to access them if I want to, without making the interface cluttered. Most importantly, everything I needed was right there in the main UI. I could log in, write a newsletter, check it, send a draft to a friend for review, and then hit send.

[Tim van Damme](https://buttondown.com/blog/mvkb)

## What’s Markdown?
Markdown is a simple way of writing that gives you all of the richness of a full-fledged email editor, directly in your document. For example, instead of clicking a passage and bolding it, you add `**asterisks**` to your text, and Buttondown will automatically bold the text for you.

Markdown was created by [John Gruber](https://daringfireball.net) in 2004, and has quickly become widespread thanks to its simple goal:

> The overriding design goal is to make [Markdown] as readable as possible… a Markdown-formatted document should be publishable as-is, as plain text, without looking like it’s been marked up with tags or formatting instructions.

If you’re new to Markdown, you can use [this tutorial](https://www.markdowntutorial.com) to get up to speed.

For more on how you can use Markdown, check out our **[Markdown help document](https://docs.buttondown.com/using-markdown)**.
